summary: This round fixes F1 with `isGoogleDiscoveryUrl`, which keeps test-mode Discovery fetches on the fixture. It fixes F3: GitHub is gated on a configured first-party client, and a catalog assertion checks that. It fixes F4 with a durable test of the shipped preset against Halo's client, and it pins the specification revision and makes a GitHub install failure non-fatal. It is not ready to merge. The coverage gate fails on the new GitHub failure fallback and on the deployment-gated origin line. Nothing yet confirms that the pinned real GitHub description installs within Executor's 30-second limit.

findings.body: Pinning the revision and making a GitHub install failure non-fatal (lines 1750-1754) resolves the part of this finding about blocking the other integrations. The remaining risk is the opposite outcome: the pinned full GitHub REST description may not fetch and compile inside the 30-second `addSpec` timeout. If it does not, every executor logs a warning and production never shows GitHub, and the suite still passes because both tests use a one-operation stub. Add a temp test that installs the real pinned description through `openApiPlugin` and `safeFetch`, or install path, and checks that it finishes inside the limit and produces the expected tools (for example `repos/list-for-authenticated-user`).

The new fallback that keeps other integrations usable when the GitHub specification fails is untested. Coverage marks lines 1751 and 1753 uncovered. Add a temp test in which `getOpenAPISpec` returns an Error for the GitHub description URL. It should check that the executor still starts, that the catalog contains the Google integrations without `github`, and that a later setup or RPC call still works.

Coverage marks line 149 uncovered. This line belongs to the deployment gate, which ensures that only local deployments can redirect the first-party GitHub client, which carries the client secret, to another OAuth origin. Cover the non-local branch with a temp test showing that a non-local deployment ignores `githubOAuthOrigin` and keeps `https://github.com`. If that is impractical, state an exemption reason.
